## The Paper

**Skill, Sequence, and Scoring: A Mathematical Comparison of Traditional and World Bowling Scoring Systems**

*Michael Borck*
School of Marketing and Management, Curtin University, Perth, Australia

Target journal: *Journal of Quantitative Analysis in Sports*

## Summary

This paper demonstrates, through exact combinatorial analysis and Monte Carlo simulation, that traditional and World Bowling scoring systems differ in mathematically precise and practically significant ways:

1. Traditional scoring is **sequence-sensitive** — the order of frames matters. World Bowling is commutative — order is irrelevant.
2. Traditional scoring has a **compounding reward gradient** — each consecutive strike is worth more. World Bowling is linear.
3. The scoring systems' discriminating power **crosses over at ~50% strike rate** — below this, World Bowling provides more spread; above it, traditional provides 33% more at the professional level.
4. The distinction matters most **within skill tiers** — both systems separate recreational from professional players, but only traditional scoring separates elite players who differ in streak ability.

## Reproducibility

All results in this paper are fully reproducible. The source code, data, and analysis scripts are available at:

**[github.com/michael-borck/skill-sequence-scoring](https://github.com/michael-borck/skill-sequence-scoring)**

### Requirements

```
pip install matplotlib numpy scipy pandas pytest
```

### Key files

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `src/bowling_distributions.py` | Exact score distributions via dynamic programming |
| `src/bowling_analysis.py` | Scoring functions and sequence sensitivity |
| `src/bowling_simulation.py` | Monte Carlo simulation across skill tiers |
| `src/sequence_permutations.py` | Exhaustive permutation analysis |
| `src/bowling_visualisations.py` | Figure generation (1–5) |
| `src/simulation_figures.py` | Figure generation (8–11) |
| `data/bowling_distributions.csv` | Full 0–300 score distribution tables |
| `paper/bowling_paper.qmd` | Quarto manuscript source |
